name: Elsecar atmospheric pumping engine
summary: An atmospheric beam engine of Newcomen's design installed around 1795 to 1796 to pump water out of the Elsecar colliery in South Yorkshire.
description: Newcomen-type atmospheric beam engine installed at the Elsecar engine pit to pump mine water.
tier_reason: Retain the Elsecar installation as a witness, not the origin of atmospheric pumping. Its1795 installation and1796 ledger must not become a1712 invention claim. This is a scoped consequence judgement, not a reward for documentation or representation.

impact.note: A late copy of a long-known engine type serving one colliery, with nothing later resting on it; implies tier 3, below the reviewed tier 2.

why: Water flooding the coal workings at the new Elsecar pit had to be pumped out for mining to continue.

date.label: by June 1796
date.basis: Historic England lists construction/installation as 1795, while another Historic England research record gives 1796; a 1796 colliery ledger has an engine account with March and June fuel, interpreted by Barnsley Museums as probably for this Newcomen pump.

events.statement: The Newcomen mine pump was installed for dewatering, and a 1796 colliery fuel ledger is interpreted as evidence of its operation by June 1796.
events.caveats: Installation is described as 1795 or 1796 by different Historic England records. The 1796 ledger does not identify the engine by type; Barnsley Museums treats the attribution as an assumption. A first pumping day is not established.

evidence.locator: Summary and History: engine pit and pumping
evidence.supports: Documents colliery date, Newcomen engine and its function.
Shows an alternative date to the 1795 listed-building account.

evidence.locator: 1796 ledger discussion, engine account and March/June fuel
evidence.supports: Museum interprets a dated engine fuel account as probably relating to the surviving Newcomen pump.
